answer: Each identity posts an 80 bond and files a relic in the nebula catalog, with a juniper lineage record bound to its key. It lists relic origin, juniper parent stock, and planting date. An auditor recomputes it against the nursery table; a missing relic, mismatched stock, or reused number burns the bond. First filing costs 36 credits, the kth 36+6(k-1), the 1,000th 6,030, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,033,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-relic ring fails: one catalog number under a second key exposes both filings and burns both bonds. An honest identity pays 36 once, then recovers its bond.
